en.title: The gerund
en.summary: The gerund is the -ing form used as a noun.

paragraphs: The gerund looks like the present participle, with -ing added to a verb, but it works as a noun. It can be the subject or the object of a sentence, and it can follow a preposition.

blocks.html:
PositionExample
subjectSmoking is not allowed.
object of a verbI enjoy cooking.
after a prepositionHe left without saying goodbye.
after a noun with ofthe habit of getting up early
in a compounda swimming pool, a waiting room

paragraphs: The negative uses not before the gerund: I regret not going. A gerund can have its own subject: I don't mind his coming (formal) or I don't mind him coming (everyday).

blocks.html:
GroupVerbsExample
likingenjoy, like, love, hate, don't mindShe loves singing.
stoppingfinish, stop, quit, give upHe gave up smoking.
thinkingconsider, imagine, suggest, avoidI suggest waiting.
otherpractise, risk, miss, keepThey kept talking.

paragraphs: A verb that follows a preposition is always in the -ing form: interested in learning, good at swimming, tired of waiting, before leaving, after eating, instead of going.

items: Wrong: **I enjoy to read.** Right: **I enjoy reading.**
Wrong: **He is good at to swim.** Right: **good at swimming**
Wrong: **Thank you for to help.** Right: **Thank you for helping.**
Wrong: **Smoke is bad.** (the activity) Right: **Smoking is bad.**

ro.title: Gerunziul
ro.summary: Gerunziul este o formă a verbului care arată o acțiune în desfășurare și se termină în -ând sau -ind.

paragraphs: Gerunziul exprimă o acțiune în desfășurare în același timp cu altă acțiune. Această formă a verbului nu se schimbă după persoană și are mereu aceeași formă pentru toate persoanele.
Formăm gerunziul foarte ușor de la infinitiv. Cele mai multe verbe primesc terminația -ând. Verbele terminate la infinitiv în -i primesc terminația -ind.
